questions.q: What separates blitzscaling from simply growing fast?
a: Keeping operations sustainable during the expansion
Raising as much venture capital as possible
Entering several countries at the same time
Hiring more employees than competitors
questions.why: The summary defines it as rapid growth to massive scale while remaining operationally sustainable.

questions.q: What does the Leonberger dog example illustrate about fast-growing companies?
a: Rapid growth creates strain that requires extra support
Big companies inevitably develop health problems
Growth slows naturally once a company matures
Small startups should avoid growing too large
questions.why: The dog grows so quickly that it needs exceptional food to survive the transformation.

questions.q: What makes a network more valuable, according to the summary?
a: Each new member makes it more useful to everyone
Each new member pays a higher joining fee
The network is owned by a single company
The network replaces older forms of communication
questions.why: The fax machine example shows why participants need others to be on the same network.

questions.q: Why do high gross margins matter for blitzscaling?
a: They leave more money per sale to reinvest in growth
They make the company easier to sell to investors
They reduce the need for a distribution channel
They allow the company to lower prices indefinitely
questions.why: Sales is one of the hardest parts of scaling, so extra margin funds further expansion.

questions.q: What are the two biggest growth limiters named in the summary?
a: Product-market fit and operational scalability
Brand awareness and hiring speed
Pricing strategy and government regulation
Distribution reach and network effects
questions.why: Hoffman says founders must address both from the beginning to keep growing.
